contract.purpose: Explain how Starboard starts from a GitHub project and produces inspectable repository and tool recommendations.
contract.canonicalPurpose: Starboard helps developers evaluating open-source tools find relevant repositories and tool evidence by grounding discovery in the GitHub project in front of them.
contract.audience: Developers evaluating open-source repositories and tools for software they are already building.
contract.job: Understand Starboard, preview one public project, or browse the public catalog.
contract.thesis: A warm, technical navigation chart that makes the evidence route visible before asking for trust.
contract.system: Editorial serif headings, compact mono labels, warm chart paper, navy evidence panels, coral signals, and ruled spatial rhythm.
contract.signature: The numbered repository-to-peer-to-tool evidence route shown as a navigational chart.
contract.risk: Dense evidence language could feel procedural, so the first viewport keeps one direct promise and one repository action.

performance.command: mise x node@24 -- psi-swarm run http://127.0.0.1:4316 --runs 5 --presets coverage --profile coverage --reason --output html
performance.environment: production static build served by astro preview

findings.name: Decorative grid-line background
findings.note: Removed the non-functional landing-page grid overlay after the detector pass.

answers.product: Project-aware open-source repository and tool discovery for GitHub.
answers.audience: Developers choosing tools for a project they are already building.
answers.value: Find relevant peers and tools without relying on generic popularity lists.
answers.mechanism: Start from one public repository, build a peer set, and retain the supporting repository evidence.
answers.proof: The page explains the evidence model, confidence boundaries, peer grouping, and investigation route, but does not show a completed real-project recommendation or measured accuracy.
answers.nextAction: Paste a public GitHub repository or browse Discover.
